note: Input contexts for the shipped DMN golden, each paired with the value EVERY
decision must produce under it. Both committed engine harnesses
(etc/kie-dmn-check, etc/camunda-dmn-check) read this file and fail on any
mismatch, on any decision present in the model but absent from `expect`, and
on any expectation naming a decision the model does not have.
WHY EXPECTED VALUES AND NOT JUST STATUSES. The failure this whole exercise is
about is silent: Camunda 8 tokenises a space-bearing FEEL name `annual income`
as `annual` `in` `come` and answers `true` -- a wrong NON-NULL value. Measured
(DMN-EXPORT-PROGRAM-MODEL-SPEC.md 13.2). A harness that fails only on FAILED,
SKIPPED and null passes such a file.
THE KEYS ARE FEEL NAMES, not L4 names: `annual_income`, not `annual income`.
That is the invariant under test, not an accident of the fixture.
COVERAGE. Between them these five cases fire every one of the nine <rule>
elements in the golden, plus both <defaultOutputEntry> paths. Case A alone --
which is what reg-cf.ctx.json holds, and what the harnesses used to be given --
leaves six of the nine unevaluated.
WHAT THESE CASES CANNOT CATCH, stated so absence is not read as evidence:
`annual income` and `net worth` are consumed only by `+` and `min`, both
commutative, so exchanging their two bindings is invisible to any context on
this exhibit. That is faithful to the statute (17 CFR 227.100(a)(2) is
symmetric in the two) rather than a gap in the fixture, and no additional case
can close it. Every other mis-binding does change an answer here.
